text:
maya: quick dump — ran the fastturn-prefetch prototype (local branch: fastturn-prefetch/v0.3) on llama3-13b-8bit with our standard 1k prompt suite.

maya: numbers: mean tokens/s ~ 1.7x vs baseline, p50 token latency improved ~18%, p99 increased for sequences >2k tokens by ~9%. overall observed 3% preference drop on our pairwise holdout (n=2k comparisons).

tessa: can you paste the exact runner config? curious about batch sizing + kv-warmup behavior.

maya: sure — main differences:
```
- speculative_ratio: 0.45
- warm_prefix_cache: true
- prefetch_window=8
- decode_mode: fastturn (two-stage: greedy-prefill -> sampled-fallback)
- fallback_latency_threshold_ms: 120
```
small script used to run: `python run_eval.py --model ll3-13b-q8 --prompts prompts/1k.json --mode fastturn --parallel 32`

raul: did you run any safety / hallucination checks? that 3% preference dip worries me if it's correlated with factuality.

maya: ran our standard truthfulness probes (QA pairs + RAG snippet answers). failure cases are concentrated on long-context citations and list outputs (enumerations) — seems the prefill greedy pass occasionally drops low-probability continuation tokens that later aid correctness.

jamal: got a quick diff of logits/entropy before/after? might be a calibration issue from quant + speculative sampling.

sophia: ops-bot posted canary:deploy for branch fastturn-prefetch/v0.3 to playground — link https://canary.redwood.internal/fastturn-prefetch — status: success :white_check_mark:

ops-bot: deploy 1769954400 by maya — env=canary, nodes=6-gpu, image=redwood-runtime:2026-03-18-fastturn

maya: attached quick histogram: prefill entropy lower by ~0.08 nats for top-5 tokens vs baseline. hypothesis: prefill greedy reduces hypothesis diversity, hurting edge-case phrasing.

tessa: idea — add a tiny stochasticity during prefill (temperature ~0.6 only for tokens with topk mass < 0.85) and re-run the 2k holdout. keeps speed but recovers low-prob cases.

raul: also try toggling prefetch_window to 6 and compare p99; smaller window might reduce tail regressions.

maya: will run both combos tomorrow morning. priority order: (A) temp-pre-fill, window=8 (B) temp-pre-fill, window=6 (C) greedy w/ calibrated bias correction. schedule: A by 09:30 PT.

jamal: for eval methodology let's avoid single-metric. propose: pairwise human preference (5k samples), perplexity diff on holdout, and systemic label checks for hallucinations (closed-book QA). that caught earlier regressions.

sophia: reminded to add pod labels for Dedicated runs — we need cost accounting for Optimize suggestions.

maya: logging note — when you look at the run artifacts: /mnt/evals/fastturn/v0.3/{split}/metrics.json (includes per-prompt tokens/s, per-token-latency, entropy traces).

tessa: thanks — one more ask: can you include the exact sample of failure prompts (top 50) so we can craft targeted prompts for regression tests?

maya: yes, will push to the repo under experiments/fastturn/v0.3/failures_top50.txt after the next run.

raul: if A recovers >2% win-rate and keeps >1.6x throughput, we can move to a small canary on Dedicated. otherwise keep in experimental.

maya: noted. will report back with A results and a diff of human preference ballots. :coffee:

sophia: ping me if you want infra support for a larger batch — can spin up extra nodes for a couple hours.

ops-bot: reminder — please tag releases with changelog:fastturn-prefetch and link eval artifacts for auditing.

maya: done, thanks everyone.
__notes: single-thread slack export; messages are chronological and prefixed by sender name as required
